title: Tool offer
description: The tools the host offers a run, as the session's two members: the runtime's tools (session.tools: McpTool, exactly as tools/list served them, filtered to this session's allow-list, reached only through callTool and the host's gate) and the host's own tools (session.hostTools: HostTool, run by the host on the adapter's behalf, answered in the shape a runtime answer takes). An adapter offers the model exactly these, under their served schemas (servedSchema: a tool served without an input schema ends the session; the Gemini family alone is shown the schema less a closed list of keywords, with a guardrail narrowed event per tool that lost one). The host also adds its own context tools (list_context, read_context, read_window and, in a conversation, update_plan and request_budget_increase), whose names an offered tool may not take. Read from web/src/assistant/engine.ts (McpTool, HostTool) and context/session.ts (contextualSession). Open: the session is an in-process value with no reader, and the runtime's answer is passed through as served. A host may offer propose_pack ($defs/proposePack): the adapter reads that call itself as the run's proposal and never reaches the host's execute, the instructions then tell the model to use it, the critic is not offered it, and the fenced block stays the fallback. The critic is offered only $defs/criticTools, of the runtime tools the session offers, and no host tool (agent#10).

tools.description: The runtime's tools (session.tools), each named within the ceiling.

hostTools.description: The host's tools (session.hostTools), the context tools the boundary adds included.

runtimeTool.description: A runtime tool (McpTool). No effect class is carried: the host decides what is read-only by name (runtimeToolContextPolicy and the read list in context/managed.ts).

inputSchema.description: The runtime's own JSON Schema for the arguments, passed through untouched.

hostTool.description: A host tool's declaration (HostTool, without its execute function, which never crosses). Its schema is the host's, written in the subset every family's wire carries.

effect.description: Host-declared effect, never supplied by model arguments.

interaction.description: A tool that pauses the run for the person (question: ask_user) or for the host's coordinator (delegation: delegate_tasks). The adapter emits user_question or delegation_requested, pauses, and returns no answer of its own.

delegation.description: The read-only capability this tool offers to a delegated child; absent means parent-only.

contextPolicy.description: Host-declared context retention (ContextToolPolicy), independent of topic, provider and action permission. immutable: the same arguments return the same value for this execution, so a read may be cached. reference: prefer this material in the bounded working summary.

presentation.description: Host-owned presentation, frozen when the tool is offered.

proposePack.description: The host tool through which the model delivers its proposal (packages/harness/engines/contract.ts: PROPOSE_PACK_TOOL, PROPOSE_PACK_SCHEMA). The host registers it among its hostTools under this name and with this input schema, which is in the subset every family's wire carries. The adapter reads the call's arguments as the proposal under the fence's rules (document an object, unknowns strings, kind absent or create), answers the model that it was received, and never calls the host's execute; arguments of another shape are a failed result naming what to correct (invalid-tool-input). The latest call's document is the one proposed. A fenced proposal in the same answer makes it ambiguous, refused as two fenced proposals are; a later request of the turn that fails leaves it delivered with a note (run-event.json, proposal).

document.description: The proposed pack, as a JSON object (not a JSON string).

unknowns.description: What the policy leaves open, one sentence each.

agentWireTool.description: A tool as the codex engine offers it on the agent wire (codexbridge.Tool in the start frame's request): an alias name desk_runtime_N or desk_host_N, the real name prefixed to the description, and the served schema. Closed: the Desk server decodes the start frame with unknown members refused; a request carries at most 128 tools.

inputSchema.description: The served schema, which the Desk server requires to be a JSON object whose type is object, at most 64 KiB (65536 bytes) as JSON text; a description is at most 8192 bytes, and all tools' schemas and descriptions together at most 1 MiB (codexbridge threadParams).

runtimeCeiling.description: The runtime tools any session may be allowed (ASSISTANT_TOOLS in packages/harness/host.ts). A session's allow-list is a subset; the gate refuses a call outside it on the wire. The Desk's five (runtimeToolCeiling in contract/desk/inventory.json) and, from the harness (agent#7), experimental_test_cases, which takes pack text and a matrix and reads no project file; it leaves the page only with the arguments tool-call.json $defs/testCasesArguments states, and one turn may call it at most testCallsPerTurn times (budget.json). The Runtime's other test and project tools stay off it: test_conformance (its suite argument is a local path the runtime reads), experimental_test_packs and experimental_test_graphs (they test the saved tree, not the draft, outside the rehearsal rule), get_pack and list_packs (they read the saved tree); toolGate.ts, REFUSED_RUNTIME_TOOLS.

reservedName.description: Names the host keeps for its own context tools; an offered tool that takes one ends the session.

criticTools.description: The critic's tools (agent#10; packages/harness/refutation.ts, CRITIC_TOOLS): an allow-list of the runtime's reads about the document, and the whole of what the critic may call. experimental_evaluate leaves only as a rehearsal (the gate's rewrite), and experimental_test_cases under its own bounds (tool-call.json $defs/testCasesArguments, and budget.json testCallsPerTurn, which the critic shares with the loop). The critic is offered these, of the runtime tools the session offers, in the session's order, and no host tool. Any other name it calls (the runtime's other reads, every host tool, propose_* and request_* among them, and the context tools) is refused by the shared boundary while the critic runs (context/session.ts, admit), before the tool gate and before a host tool runs: the call is not made, the model reads a permission failure, and a guardrail refused event names the tool.
